h1.cap: Staying out of it feels safe. Five hundred years ago, one man disagreed.

n2.cap: Ancient Greece. King Antiochus comes to drive out Rome. Both send envoys to the Achaeans.

n3.cap: Antiochus says... stay neutral. Rome says... take up arms.

n4.cap: Rome warns... stay out, and you get no favour. You're just the winner's prize.

q1.cap: Machiavelli saw the pattern... "he who is not your friend will demand your neutrality, whilst he who is your friend will entreat you to declare yourself…"

n5.cap: Team meeting. Two plans. Both leads look at you... you say, both are good.

n6.cap: Plan A wins. Its lead remembers you didn't help. The other... remembers you didn't either.

q2.cap: Machiavelli, bluntly... "irresolute princes, to avoid present dangers, generally follow the neutral path, and are generally ruined."

n7.cap: Is picking a side safe? No path is perfectly safe, he admits. Choose the lesser risk... eyes open.

n8.cap: Taking a side isn't taking a swing. It's saying where you stand... and why.

n9.cap: Tonight, one choice you keep dodging with "either is fine"... give your real answer. Kindly, with a reason.

n10.cap: When did staying neutral cost you? Tell us below.

n11.cap: Follow Awazzzz... we don't sit on the fence.
